name: Fertiliser supply
value: Egypt urea $535/t FOB; gas cuts up to 33%
summary: Egypt raised gas curtailments on fertiliser plants to 33% on 9 Nov; Egyptian urea near $535 a tonne, up 17% since Sep
state: Egypt raised gas curtailments on fertiliser and methanol plants to 33% from 20%, confirmed by Mopco on 8 Nov, with no end date, as LNG import costs surged; Egyptian granular urea for November is about $535 a tonne FOB, up 17% from September (Enterprise, 9 Nov). US retail urea averaged $662 a ton in the week to 6 Nov, 11% above a year earlier (DTN). No 60% three-month rise or closed route was found as of 12 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Farmers buying nitrogen fertiliser for spring are exposed to higher costs, which can feed into food prices later.
rubric_hit: Watch: Gulf export route via Hormuz impeded and Egyptian supply curtailed; urea +17% since Sep, below 60% Alert line

sources.title: Enterprise — Gov't deepens industrial gas rationing, raising curtailments on fertilizer and methanol plants to 33%
DTN — Retail fertilizer prices mixed during first week of November

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
